question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: text -> QUOTE(text): a quotation mark, each character of the text rendered by TABLE ESCAPE in order, a quotation mark. bool -> "true" or "false".
list -> "[" + the renderings of its elements, in order, separated by "," + "]". The empty list -> "[]".
map -> "{" + one entry per key in KEY ORDER (R4), separated by ",", each entry QUOTE(key) + ":" + the rendering of its value + "}". The empty map -> "{}". Keys escape exactly as text (R1).

KEY ORDER is ascending lexicographic comparison of the keys as sequences of 16-bit code units, a proper prefix sorting first; a character outside the basic multilingual plane counts as its two surrogate code units (lead unit in 0xD800..0xDBFF). This is NOT scalar-value order: a key holding an astral character sorts BEFORE a key holding a character in 0xE000..0xFFFF at the same position ("😀" before "" before "￿"); both orders agree everywhere below 0xD800. Digit-spelled keys sort as text ("10" before "2"). CITED ANCHOR SIR_SCHEMA §10 — keys sort by 16-bit code units

f64 PROJECTION. A map whose key "t" holds exactly the text "f64" must have key "bits" holding text of exactly 16 characters, each a digit or a LOWER-case letter a..f; otherwise -> throws (absent, not text, 15 or 17 characters, upper-case hex). A valid one renders as "{\"bits\":" + QUOTE(bits) + ",\"t\":\"f64\"}". Every other entry, "v" included, is dropped WITHOUT being examined: a raw number or none under a dropped key does not throw. CITED FIDELITY package
throw PROJECTION. A map whose key "t" holds exactly the text "throw" renders as "{\"t\":\"throw\"}"; every other entry, the message included, is dropped without being examined. CITED FIDELITY package

The projections test only the exact text value of key "t" (case and whitespace significant; a list holding "f64" or a bool there does not match) and apply to EVERY map at every depth, inside lists and inside other maps' values. A list is never projected. Every other tag ("text", "map", "list", "i64", "none", "record", "bytes", ...) is an ordinary map under R3.

A raw f64 (any value, NaN and -0 included) or a none reached anywhere by R1-R3 -> throws: the whole call throws and yields no text. That it throws is the observation; the message is a display hint, not part of the contract.
The result contains no whitespace or separator outside quoted text: no space after "," or ":", no newline.

NESTING CAP. Every node the rendering visits has a depth: the whole value is depth 0, and each element of a list and each value of a map is one deeper than the list or map holding it (keys are not nodes). Visiting a node deeper than 416 -> throws; 416 = 4 x 100 + 16, the codec's 100-value cap at up to four raw levels per typed value, plus 16 (TABLE DIALS). Only visited nodes count: entries dropped by R5 and R6 are never visited at any depth, while the entries a projection renders ("bits" and "t") sit one level below the projected map. So a text or bool at depth 416 renders and at 417 throws; an empty list or map at depth 416 renders and at 417 throws; an f64- or throw-tagged map at depth 416 throws, at 415 renders; a typed list chain {"t":"list","v":[...]} costs two depths per level. The check precedes every other rule at a node: a too-deep node throws whatever it holds. CITED FIDELITY package
MAX_VALUE_DEPTH  -> 100; the codec's value-nesting cap (this unit never checks it; it sizes RAW_CAP)
RAW_CAP          -> 416; 4 x MAX_VALUE_DEPTH + 16, the deepest node depth that renders
quotation mark                                       -> "\""
reverse solidus                                      -> "\\"
backspace 0x08                                       -> "\b"
form feed 0x0C                                       -> "\f"
line feed 0x0A                                       -> "\n"
carriage return 0x0D                                 -> "\r"
any other control character 0x00..0x1F               -> "\u00" + two LOWER-case hex digits (0x1F -> "\u001f")
an unpaired surrogate code unit (js widening only)   -> "\u" + four LOWER-case hex digits (0xD800 -> "\ud800")
anything else, delete 0x7F, solidus "/", 0x2028, 0x2029 and every non-ASCII scalar included -> itself, unescaped
